label: Job offer / employment contract
source: Indian Contract Act, 1872 and Code on Wages, 2019, plus common Indian employment practice. Verify against the current law before relying on it.

rules.title: No post-exit non-compete
rules.benchmark: Under Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, a clause that stops you working for others after you leave is void. Restrictions during the job are allowed.
rules.flag: A non-compete that applies after you leave is against the law.

rules.title: Reasonable training bond
rules.benchmark: A bond can recover only reasonable, actual training costs (Section 74, Indian Contract Act). A fixed penalty unrelated to real costs is generally unenforceable.
rules.flag: A large fixed bond or exit penalty is unusual.

rules.title: Equal notice period
rules.benchmark: Notice should be the same for both sides; 30 to 90 days is common practice.
rules.flag: The employer giving much less notice than you must give is unusual.

rules.title: Wages can't be withheld
rules.benchmark: Earned wages can't be withheld as a penalty. The Code on Wages, 2019 requires dues to be paid within two working days of leaving.
rules.flag: Withholding earned salary or delaying final dues is against the law.

rules.title: IP limited to the job
rules.benchmark: The employer may own work made for the job. Claiming your personal projects made outside work, with your own resources, is unusual.
rules.flag: Claiming all inventions, including personal-time work, is unusual.

rules.title: Changes need consent
rules.benchmark: Changes to salary, role or location should need your written consent.
rules.flag: The employer changing pay, role or location at its sole discretion is unusual.

rules.title: Working hours and overtime
rules.benchmark: The common legal standard is 48 hours a week, with extra hours paid as overtime.
rules.flag: Long fixed hours with no overtime pay are unusual.
